question: When a non-compliant traffic control device is replaced because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable, what is the general rule and the limited replacement-in-kind exception?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The general rule is that when a non-compliant device is being replaced or refurbished because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable, it must be replaced with a compliant device. The limited exception permits replacement in kind when engineering judgment shows it is more appropriate—either because a single compliant device amid a series of adjacent non-compliant devices would confuse road users, and/or because the scheduled replacement of the whole series will still achieve timely MUTCD compliance. Standards (mandatory): - "A non-compliant traffic control device that is being replaced or refurbished because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02) for any reason shall be replaced with a compliant device, except as provided for in Paragraph 13 of this Section." - "Unless a particular device is no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02), non-compliant devices on existing highways and bikeways shall be brought into compliance with the current edition of the National MUTCD as part of the systematic upgrading of substandard traffic control devices (and installation of new required traffic control devices) required pursuant to the Highway Safety Program, 23 U.S.C. §402(a)." - In the temporary traffic control context: "Channelizing devices that are no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02) shall be replaced." Guidance (recommended): - Agencies should establish "maintenance policies that incorporate effective practices to identify and then fix or replace in a timely manner any traffic control device that is reaching the end of its useful life, or that is damaged or otherwise no longer serviceable." - Functional maintenance of traffic control devices should be used to determine if certain devices need to be changed to meet current traffic conditions. Options (permitted): - A non-compliant traffic control device may be replaced in kind when engineering judgment indicates it is more appropriate because: (A) one compliant device in the midst of a series of adjacent non-compliant devices would be confusing to road users, and/or (B) the schedule for replacement of the whole series of non-compliant devices will result in achieving timely compliance with the MUTCD. Visual evidence: [Image 5] shows the full text of Section 1B.03, including the Standard requiring replacement with a compliant device (Paragraph 12) and the Option describing the replacement-in-kind exception (Paragraph 13). Citations: - Section 1B.03 Standard §12 (p.6) - Section 1B.03 Option §13 (p.6) - Section 1B.03 Standard §5 (p.5) - Section 6K.01 Standard §15 (p.815) - Section 5A.04 Guidance §6 (p.762) - Section 1D.10 Guidance §1 (p.38) - Page 47
gold_answer: The replacement must generally be a compliant device. A non-compliant device may be replaced in kind only when engineering judgment finds that a lone compliant device among adjacent non-compliant devices would confuse users and/or the planned replacement schedule for the whole series will achieve timely compliance.
